title: The 1929 Deed in Which Spedan Lewis Signed Away His Profits
conflicts: Income gap: the Guardian's 1963 obituary quotes Partnership for All (£26,000 to the three Lewises against £16,000 for all other staff), the Partnership says only 'more than all employees together', and some summaries say 'equal'; the story gives his own figures, attributed. Profit-sharing start: 1920 (Partnership, Guardian, Portsmouth case) against 1919 (BBC 2002); 1920 used. Oswald's 1926 share: 'gave' (Partnership) against 'bought with a bank loan' (Wikipedia, citing Cox 2010); story says neutrally 'took over'.
notes: The Partnership's Memory Store pages (jlpmemorystore.org.uk) return 403 and the Internet Archive was unreachable from this machine, so the Partnership's careers-site history and corporate heritage page are cited for the trust-settlement details. £1 million in bonds over 30 years is attributed to the Partnership's own account. Repeat screen flagged a Copia edition (Jonathan Lewis, a different person) but let it through; no fields were reworded. Quote stance: complicates.
